about: Tier c's read classifier fixtures (process_trap.py `reads_of`): each case a bash command as the model sends it, with ROOT standing for the run's Lite checkout, and the reads it makes of that checkout, each a path relative to it ('' for the checkout itself). `reads: []` is a known non-read. Modelled on the interviews smoke run's audited commands (the audit's section 4 classes), written fresh, never copied. `facts`, where given, are the facts the command targets. A case's `root`, where given, is the checkout as the grader is handed it, and HOME stands for a home directory: an assembled log writes home paths as `~` (scripts/scrub.py), a raw one spells them out, and either may meet either form of the root.

reads.why: an absolute cat of a source file
a relative cat after cd into the source (the audit's 45392)
orientation: listing the checkout, then its parts, after cd
reads.cmd: ls ROOT; cd ROOT && ls packages; ls docs

reads.why: a grep with its pattern and a relative path after cd (the audit's GA class)
a keyword search targets its fact by the pattern
a grep with no path searches the working directory
sed -n prints part of a file: a read
head with an option value is not a path
a docs read
a read piped on: the grep reads only its input
git show of a source file at HEAD is a read of the checkout
a page script fetching a source file over /@fs/ (the sealed smoke's 11689)
reads.cmd: chrome-devtools evaluate_script "async () => { const f = await (await fetch('/@fsROOT/packages/babylon-lite/src/scene/scene-core.ts')).text(); return f.length; }" --pageId 1

reads.why: a /@fs/ base joined with a file name in the script
reads.cmd: chrome-devtools evaluate_script "async () => { const base = '/@fs/ROOT/packages/babylon-lite/src/'; const f = await (await fetch(base + 'scene/scene-core.ts')).text(); return f.slice(0, 100); }" --pageId 1

reads.why: a dynamic import of a source module over /@fs/
reads.cmd: chrome-devtools evaluate_script "async () => { const m = await import('/@fs/ROOT/packages/babylon-lite/src/picking/ray.ts'); return Object.keys(m); }" --pageId 1

reads.why: a read after a heredoc write in the same call
reads.cmd:
cat > main.ts <<'EOF'
const x = 1;
EOF
cat ROOT/packages/babylon-lite/src/scene/visibility.ts

an assembled log's tilde listing, graded against an absolute root
a raw log's absolute cd, graded against a tilde root
a tilde cd, then a relative search

an assembled log's /@fs~/ import, graded against an absolute root
a listing whose errors are discarded: the redirection is no operand, so ls still lists where it stands
a search written to a file: the redirection's target is written, never read
reads.cmd: cd ROOT && grep -rn setMeshVisible packages > out.txt

an input redirection is a read of its file
errors folded into the pipe
a cat appended to a file
an input redirection with its file attached

a heredoc fed to python3 opens a Lite doc
